Thanks for the ping. Technical summary below — happy to refine language for auditors.

1) Propagation windows (high-level):
- Hot region replicas: deletion tombstone is written synchronously to primary and replicated to region peers within 0–5s under normal conditions; worst-case replication lag during high load or network partition observed up to ~30s.
- Cold/offsite snapshots: we maintain scheduled snapshot jobs (incremental) with a default cadence of 4 hours for production accounts; deletion markers are recorded at snapshot creation time, so a deletion will be reflected in the next snapshot capture window (typical 0–4 hours; worst-case up to 8 hours if a job is delayed).
- Cross-region DR copies: cross-region snapshot replication is asynchronous; typical propagation completes within 15–45 minutes, worst-case up to 3 hours under heavy transfer congestion or throttling.

2) Legal hold behaviour: snapshots continue to be created while a legal hold (preserve flag) is active. Snapshots associated with preserved datasets are marked with a preserve tag and are excluded from the background expunge process. We track the preserve flag on the snapshot metadata (snapshot_id + preserve=true) and that is included in the audit manifest.

3) Restores & point-in-time semantics: restores use the last consistent snapshot prior to the restore target time. If a deletion happened at T_del and you request a restore to T_restore where T_restore < T_del, the deleted object will be present in the restore. If T_restore >= T_del the object will not be present. Because cold snapshots are incremental, we include the snapshot id and sequence number in the restore manifest so you can show the exact retention point.

4) Audit artefacts we can provide:
- Deletion event log (RFC3339 timestamps, request id, user id)
- Snapshot manifest (snapshot_id, creation_time, sequence range, preserve flag)
- Storage manifest for cross-region replication (replica ids, transfer completion timestamps)
- Internal tombstone index entries (forensic view showing marker creation and eventual expunge)

I'll attach the DR/retention matrix and a sample audit checklist. Note: the matrix shows typical and max windows — for SLA-backed Dedicated customers we can provide narrower bounds depending on reserved capacity and configured snapshot cadence.

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Summary below for your auditors and Legal Ops; attaching the matrix and checklist referenced by Karthik.

Short answers:
- Deletions appear in hot replicas within seconds (0–5s typical, up to ~30s worst-case).
- Deletions are captured by the next scheduled offsite snapshot (default 4-hour cadence; typical 0–4h, worst-case ~8h if delayed).
- Cross-region DR replication is asynchronous (typical 15–45m, worst-case ~3h).
- During legal hold, snapshots are tagged and excluded from expunge — yes, snapshot creation continues.
- For restores we use the last consistent snapshot prior to the target time; deleted objects are present if you restore to a time before deletion.
- Audit artefacts we can provide: deletion event logs, snapshot manifests (with preserve flags), replication transfer records, and a tombstone index excerpt.
